newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO delays decision on Japan liquor tax till Fri.
newsitem.headline: WTO delays decision on Japan liquor tax till Fri.

text.p: The World Trade Organisation's Dispute Settlement Body on Tuesday postponed until Friday a decision on whether to adopt a panel ruling on the Japanese liquor tax on foreign imports, a spokesman said.
The meeting was "suspended because there was not a simple majority of WTO's 125 members present, he added. There were only 37 of the needed 63 members present for the closed-door talks.
It was the first time the WTO Dispute Settlement Body was forced to postpone action due a lack of a quorum.

The WTO, ruling on a complaint by the European Union, the United States and Canada, found that Japan's taxes on imported spirits unfairly compared with a domestic liquor known as shochu. The tax has been at issue for nearly a decade.
"The meeting is suspended and is being reconvened on Friday, November 1," a spokesman said. "There was a lack of a quorum."
Japan's ambassador Nobutoshi Akao said that given the importance of the decision, his delegation preferred that WTO rules of procedure be followed and a quorum be present.
"In light of the rules of procedure, this number is very insufficient for the board to make a very important decision," Akao told Reuters.
"We fully respect this rule (of procedure)," he added.
There was no immediate comment from the EU delegation, headed by Ian Wilkinson.
Brazil's ambassador Celso Lafer, who serves as DSB chairman, consulted the Japanese and EU delegations during a 50-minute break in Tuesday's meeting to try to resolve the hold-up.
But he could not convince Japan's delegation to allow the report to be adopted by a consensus of 37 delegations, according to trade sources. "This is not a good precedent," said one.
